Spider-Man: Brand New Day.text: Its title comes from a 2008 comic storyline that reset Spider-Man's status quo.
Spider-Man: Brand New Day.evidence: Sony was developing a fourth MCU Spider-Man film by August 2019, and producer Amy Pascal revealed in November 2021 that it was intended to be the first in a new trilogy starring Holland. ... Cretton was hired to direct by October 2024, and the title—derived from the 2008 comic book storyline "Brand New Day" that reset Spider-Man's status quo—was announced in March 2025.

Star Wars: The Force Awakens.text: It was the first Star Wars film not to extensively involve George Lucas, who only consulted early on.
Star Wars: The Force Awakens.evidence: The film is the first Star Wars film to not extensively involve franchise creator George Lucas, who only served as a creative consultant in the early stages of production.

Avengers: Endgame.text: It out-grossed Infinity War's entire theatrical run in just eleven days.
Avengers: Endgame.evidence: It grossed $2.8 billion worldwide during its initial theatrical run, surpassing Infinity War's entire theatrical run in eleven days, setting several box-office records, and surpassing Avatar (2009) to become the highest-grossing film of all time.

Spider-Man: No Way Home.text: Marvel Studios left the project in 2019, but fan backlash led to a new deal with Sony a month later.
Spider-Man: No Way Home.evidence: Negotiations between Sony and Marvel Studios to alter their deal—in which they produce the Spider-Man films together—ended with Marvel Studios leaving the project in August 2019, but a negative fan reaction led to a new deal between the companies a month later.

Avatar.text: James Cameron wrote an 80-page treatment in 1994, then waited for the technology to catch up.
Avatar.evidence: Development of Avatar began in 1994, when Cameron wrote an 80-page treatment for the film. Filming was due to take place after the completion of Cameron's 1997 film Titanic, for a planned release in 1999; however, according to Cameron, the necessary technology was not yet available to achieve his vision of the film.

Top Gun: Maverick.text: During the pandemic Tom Cruise had every streaming offer turned down, insisting on a theatrical release.
Top Gun: Maverick.evidence: During the pandemic, several streaming companies attempted to purchase the streaming rights to the film from Paramount, but all offers were declined on the orders of Cruise, who insisted that it should be released exclusively in theaters.

Black Panther.text: Wesley Snipes planned to make a Black Panther film back in 1992.
Black Panther.evidence: Wesley Snipes planned to make a Black Panther film in 1992, but the project did not come to fruition.

Avatar: The Way of Water.text: It was delayed for years partly by the need for new technology to film motion capture underwater.
Avatar: The Way of Water.evidence: However, the addition of two more sequels—for a total of five films—and the need to develop new technology to film motion-capture scenes underwater, led to significant delays.

Avengers: Infinity War.text: The story draws on Jim Starlin's 1991 comic book The Infinity Gauntlet.
Avengers: Infinity War.evidence: The Russo brothers came on board to direct in April 2015, and a month later, Markus and McFeely signed on to write the script for the film, which draws inspiration from Jim Starlin's 1991 comic book The Infinity Gauntlet and Jonathan Hickman's 2013 comic book Infinity.

Titanic.text: Production began on 1 September 1995 with James Cameron shooting footage of the real wreck.
Titanic.evidence: Production began on September 1, 1995, when Cameron shot footage of the Titanic wreck.
